items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped from availability check straight into building the move profile
Never asked 'How are you today?' at the open

Started to ask home size ('How many bedrooms are we focusing on?') then cut himself off and never got the answer — later admitted 'I was working under that assumption' about it being a one-bedroom equivalent, which is the number the whole 3-hour estimate rests on
No 'Pricing is super simple' opener before quoting the rate
Never delivered the full 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees)
Did not state disassembly/reassembly is included, despite two queen beds on the inventory
Did not list what's included beyond wrap and pads — no gas, truck, taxes, tools
Never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
Did not tell the customer the confirmation email has a bolded detail list at the top or ask them to reply with corrections
Did not give business hours or a general callback path beyond 'ask for me'
No packing-services question and no packing pricing mentioned
No access/parking questions, no long-walk or narrow-hallway questions, no walk-distance factor in the estimate
Never asked the moving-stressors question — and the customer surfaced two real concerns unprompted at the very end (elderly mother, brand-new home) that should have come out during probing
Used the customer's name almost never — defaulted to 'boss', 'boss man', 'Mister'
top_strength: The estimate build was genuinely strong: he gave a real time range (2.5–3.5 hrs), named movers and truck count, explained the 2.5-hour minimum with 15-minute prorating, then explicitly padded to 3 hours and told the customer why — wiggle room to help his mom place furniture. He also proactively cleared the trip fee once he had both addresses and handled the No Worries coverage twice, in plain language, with a sense-check.
coaching_note: He never established home size — he asked 'how many bedrooms' and then talked over his own question, so the 3-hour estimate is built on an inventory list plus his own guess that it's 'the equivalent of a one bedroom apartment.' That is exactly the pattern that blows estimate accuracy. Coach him to finish the question he starts and get the sq ft or bedroom count on record before pricing anything. Second: the Save Your Ass speech was completely absent on a call where it would have paid off immediately — an elderly customer with 15 boxes and a son who is out of town is the ideal candidate for the consolidate-and-take-a-carload prep talk.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and patient — 'take your time', 'no need to apologize' when the customer stopped to check with his mom — plus a genuine rapport moment on the Maserati/Mazer Drive joke and a customer who ended the call complimenting the company's reputation.
